date.as_written: nepāle śaśivāṇabhūtasahite nepālasamvatsare āṣāḍhe śitapakṣavahnitithike sayyāsane vūddhike | āditye

notes: The Kundamālā's author appears as 'kāvar(!) dvāranāgasya'. Read 'kāvar' as kaveḥ ('of the poet'). The play is usually attributed to Dhīranāga, sometimes to Diṅnāga. Dvāranāga is probably a corruption of Dhīranāga; it is kept as written. Chronogram: śaśi = 1, vāṇa = 5, bhūta = 5. Read right to left this gives NS 551 (c. 1431 CE), which matches the catalogue. vahnitithi means tṛtīyā (the 3rd); śitapakṣa means śuklapakṣa (the bright half); āditye means Sunday. 'sayyāsane' (śayyāsane?) is unclear. It may be a corrupt nakṣatra name or part of the wordplay in the verse. 'vūddhike' probably refers to the yoga Vṛddhi. The date verse plays on the subject of the play, Sītā's banishment. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The other colophons in the manuscript (Rāmāyaṇasāvitrī, Pañcavaktrastuti, Hariharātmakastava from the Harivaṃśa) contain no personal data.
